rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Pharaoh’s destruction, Israel was told to settle in Egypt and Syria; at the final promise all will be brought from graves to the Resurrection mixed together, with no tribal recognition.
rows.anchor: من بعده أي من بعد هلاك فرعون وقومه لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض يعني مصر والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lafīfan evokes troops mixed together; the root describes things intermingling and joining.
rows.anchor: وهو من قول الجيوش إذا اختلطوا، وكل شيء اختلط بشيء تعطف به والتف.

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: They gloss lafīfan as ‘all together’; its singular can predicate a plural because it is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك: (لفيفا) أي جميعا، ووحد اللفيف وهو خبر عن الجمع

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He identifies the final promise with Jesus son of Mary descending from heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة يعني مجيء عيسى ابن مريم من السماء

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: He glosses the people brought together as coming from here and there, all together.
rows.anchor: وقال البزار: من هاهنا وهاهنا، يقول: جميعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Moses story consoles Muhammad: as Pharaoh tried to expel Moses and Israel, Meccans sought to expel Muhammad; God saved Israel and would likewise give Muhammad victory.
rows.anchor: وهذه القصة تعزية لنبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وتقوية لقلبه، يقول الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran was sent down and descended with truth; Muhammad was sent only as bearer of glad tidings and warning.
rows.anchor: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل يعني القرآن وما أرسلناك يا محمد إلا مبشرا ونذيرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran was revealed as a recitation and divided into parts.
rows.anchor: وقرآنا فرقناه أي وأنزلناه قرآنا ففصلناه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He reads farraqnahu with doubled rāʾ: the Quran was divided because it was not revealed all at once, but in installments over twenty years; Ubayy’s reading adds ‘upon you.’
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس: فرقناه بالتشديد وقال: لأنه لم ينزل مرة واحدة

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: Other reciters read the verb lightly, likening it to the wording that every wise matter is distinguished.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتخفيف كقوله فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as ‘explained it’; al-Hasan says God distinguished truth from falsehood through it, and other readers say ‘made it clear.’
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس فصلناه، قال الحسن: فرق الله به بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gradual recitation lets people hear it at a measured, gentle pace over twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: لتقرأه على الناس على مكث أي تؤدة ومهل في ثلاث وعشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge before the Quran’s revelation and Muhammad’s appearance are believing People of Scripture; when it is recited they prostrate on their faces, and its descent increases their humility.
rows.anchor: إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله أي من قبل نزول القرآن وخروج محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ‘Chins’ means their faces, which they place in prostration.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس أراد الوجوه سجدا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They are People of Scripture who, hearing what was revealed to Muhammad, prostrated and affirmed that their Lord’s promise had indeed been fulfilled.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: هم ناس من أهل الكتاب حين سمعوا ما أنزل على محمد

rows.speaker: عبد الأعلى التيمي
rows.claim: Knowledge that does not make its possessor weep is unlikely to be beneficial; he recited this verse and compared it with 19:58.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الأعلى التيمي: من أوتي من العلم ما لا يبكيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The verse was revealed after Muhammad prayed at night and invoked Allah, Rahman, and Rahim in prostration; polytheists alleged he invoked two gods and associated Rahman with Musaylima of Yamama.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تهجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات ليلة فجعل يقول في سجوده:

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Muhammad first wrote ‘In Your name, O God’; after the basmala in Solomon’s letter was revealed he wrote the full basmala, prompting Arabs to ask what al-Rahman meant.
rows.anchor: قال ميمون بن مهران: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في أول ما أوحي إليه يكتب:

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: People of Scripture objected that Muhammad mentioned al-Rahman little although the Torah uses the name often; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: قال أهل الكتاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever of these two names—or any of God’s names—one invokes, the Most Beautiful Names belong to Him; ayyāmanā means ‘whichever you invoke.’
rows.anchor: أيا ما تدعوا من هذين الاسمين ومن جميع أسمائه فله الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muhammad’s loud recitation let polytheists hear and insult the Quran, its sender, and reciter; the middle course lets companions hear without exposing him to abuse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى بأصحابه رفع صوته بالقرآن،

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Muhammad used to recite aloud in the Sacred Mosque; Quraysh asked him not to do so lest he offend their gods and threatened to revile his Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يجهر بقراءة القرآن في المسجد الحرام،

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: At Abu Sufyan’s house near Safa, Abu Jahl told Muhammad not to fabricate about God; when Muhammad lowered his voice, Abu Jahl boasted he had silenced him, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي في دار أبي سفيان بن حرب عند الصفا،

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Abu Bakr whispered to privately address God, while Umar recited loudly to drive away Satan and awaken the Lord; the verse made Abu Bakr raise his voice slightly and Umar lower his.
rows.anchor: وروى [علقمة] عن ابن سيرين في هذه الآية قال: كان أبو بكر

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: She says the verse concerned the tashahhud, when a Bedouin recited it loudly.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي (رضي الله عنه) : نزلت هذه الآية في التشهد،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Do not use prayer publicly for show, nor neglect it in private.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: [لا تراء] بصلاتك في العلانية ولا [تسئها] في السر.

rows.speaker: الوالبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The command means neither pray ostentatiously before people nor abandon prayer out of fear of them.
rows.anchor: الوالبي عن ابن عباس: لا تصل مرائيا الناس، ولا تدعها مخافة الناس،

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: People of Scripture whispered so softly no letter was heard; God forbids shouting like them or whispering like them, and Gabriel taught the middle way in prayer.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: كان أهل الكتاب يخافتون في الصلاة، لم يجهر أحدهم بالحرف

rows.speaker: علي والنخعي ومجاهد وابن مكحول
rows.claim: They apply the command to supplication rather than ritual recitation.
rows.anchor: وقال: علي والنخعي ومجاهد وابن مكحول: هي في الدعاء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
rows.claim: When Bedouins of Banu Tamim asked God for provision after Muhammad’s prayer, he asked whether they were shouting, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن شداد: كان أعراب من بني تميم إذا سلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: شيخ من أصحاب رسول الله
rows.claim: A Companion says the verse concerns supplication: do not raise the voice while seeking forgiveness; recall sins quietly so others do not hear and repeat them.
rows.anchor: أن شيخا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حدثه أن رسول الله قال في هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khafata can describe a dead person when the body has cooled; the prescribed course lies between loudness and whispering.
rows.anchor: ومنه يقال للميت إذا برد خفت. وابتغ بين ذلك أي بين الجهر والإخفات سبيلا

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: The praise means God made the speaker know that He has taken no child.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل: يعني الذي عرفني أنه لم يتخذ ولدا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: God has no ally from humiliation: He is not humbled and does not need an ally to strengthen Him.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: لم يذل فيحتاج الى ولي يتعزز به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To magnify God is to declare Him above having a partner or an ally.
rows.anchor: وكبره تكبيرا وعظمه أن يكون له شريك أو ولي،

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: A servant’s saying ‘God is greatest’ is better than the world and everything in it.
rows.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: قول العبد: «الله أكبر» خير من الدنيا

rows.speaker: سهل بن معاذ عن أبيه
rows.claim: The Prophet called this passage, through its end, the verse of honor.
rows.anchor: وروى سهل بن معاذ عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده
rows.claim: The Prophet taught this verse seven times to a boy from Banu Abd al-Muttalib as soon as the child could speak clearly.
rows.anchor: قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أفصح الغلام من بني عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: محمد بن سلمة
rows.claim: He reports that reciting the end of Surat al-Isra earns a reward filling the heavens and earth, linked to God’s condemnation of claiming He has a child.
rows.anchor: وروى محمد بن سلمة عن عبد الحميد بن واصل قال: من قرأ آخر بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses the upright book as just.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: عدلا.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The Quran is upright over all scriptures and abrogates their laws.
rows.anchor: الفراء: قيما على الكتب كلها ناسخا لشرائعها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is straight and free of contradiction; it warns of severe punishment and gives believers glad tidings of Paradise and an everlasting reward.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب قيما مستقيما. قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mākithīn means remaining there forever; the warning is directed to those who claim God has a child without knowledge themselves or their ancestors.
rows.anchor: ماكثين: مقيمين فيه أبدا. وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaburat kalimatan is accusative as specification or interruption, with implied ‘the word has become great’; their claim is only a lie.
rows.anchor: كبرت كلمة نصب على التمييز والقطع، تقديره: كبرت الكلمة كلمة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bākhiʿ means destroying yourself from grief, sorrow, and anger over their failure to believe in the Quran.
rows.anchor: فلعلك باخع نفسك: قاتل نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything on earth is its adornment; al-Dahhak narrows this to flourishing plants, and the trial asks who is most ascetic toward it.
rows.anchor: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض من كل شيء زينة لها، قال الضحاك من الزاكية خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will make the earth level, barren, dry, smooth, and unable to grow anything.
rows.anchor: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا: مستويا جرزا: يابسا أملس لا تنبت شيئا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am ḥasibta means ‘rather, did you think?’ The Companions of the Cave and Inscription are not God’s most astonishing signs; creation of the heavens and earth is more extraordinary.
rows.anchor: أم حسبت، معناه: بل أم حسبت، يعني: أظننت يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kahf is a mountain cave; the passage reports a Prophetic story of three travelers trapped by a rock, each invoking a good deed.
rows.anchor: والكهف هو الغار في الجبل. واختلفوا في الرقيم، فقال فيه ما

rows.speaker: ابن عمر عن رسول الله
rows.claim: In the cave story, one man had paid a worker fully for half a day’s work; the worker left his wages, which the employer invested until they grew into cattle, then returned in full.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن ثلاثة نفر خرجوا يرتادون لأهلهم،

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read tatazāwar lightly, dropping one zāy; the Syrian tazūr has the pattern of taḥmar. Both mean the sun inclines away from the cave.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة بالتخفيف على حذف أحد الزاءين، وقرأ أهل الشام: تزور على وزن تحمر،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses taqriḍuhum as leaving them; Muqatil says it passes beyond them. Qaraḍ originally means cutting.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تدعهم. قال مقاتل بن حيان: تجاوزهم. وأصل القرض: القطع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajwah is a spacious part of the cave, with plural forms fajawāt and faja.
rows.anchor: وهم في فجوة منه، أي متسع من الكهف، وجمعها فجوات وفجى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed them in an airy, spacious spot facing the Pleiades so the sun missed them at dawn and dusk, sparing them heat, faded complexions, worn clothes, and the cave’s oppressive air.
rows.anchor: فأعلمنا أنه بوأهم في مغناة من الكهف مستقبلا بنات نعش، تميل عنهم الشمس طالعة وغاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At a meeting with the Prophet, Najran’s Christian leaders differed: Sayyid, a Jacobite, said three; al-Aqib, a Nestorian, said five; Muslims said seven. The Quran confirms the Muslim view.
rows.anchor: أن السيد والعاقب وأصحابهما من نصارى أهل نجران كانوا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb means conjecture without certainty; the cited poem witnesses this sense of rajm.
rows.anchor: أي قذفا بالظن من غير يقين، كقول الشاعر: وأجعل مني الحق غيبا مرجما

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view calls the conjunction before ‘eight’ the waw of eight: Arabs counted in groups of seven, as illustrated by three Quranic passages.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذه الواو واو الثمانية، إن العرب يقولون: واحد، اثنان، ثلاثة،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view calls it a waw of judgment and confirmation: the quotation ends at ‘seven,’ then the text confirms the dog was eighth, supporting the Muslim count.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذه واو الحكم والتحقيق، فكأنه حكى اختلافهم فتم الكلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says only a few people know the sleepers’ number.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: قليل من الناس.

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He identifies the few who know the number as People of Scripture.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: يعني بالقليل: أهل الكتاب.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says he himself is one of the few who know their number.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى. ما يعلمهم إلا قليل قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven sleepers are listed by name; their brindled dog is Qitmir, a breed between a Qalti and a Kurdish dog. Muhammad ibn al-Musayyib calls the Qalti Chinese.
rows.anchor: وهم: مكسلمينا، وتمليخا، ومرطونس ، وسارينوس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not dispute their number or ask People of Scripture; the Quran’s account is enough, and discussion should stay with what it plainly tells.
rows.anchor: فلا تمار فيهم، أي في عدتهم وشأنهم إلا مراء ظاهرا وهو ما قص عليه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Mahil is melted, bubbling gold and silver or something brought to its greatest heat; al-Muntafiʿ describes it as an intensely red ember-like bread crust, while ṭulyā is a tar-coated camel.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: المهل الذي قد انتهى حره.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The people of Hell eat Zaqqum until their skin and faces fall away; boiling drink then roasts the exposed flesh when brought to their mouths.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: إذا جاع أهل النار استغاثوا بشجرة الزقوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء
rows.claim: They gloss the Fire’s resting place as an abode, gathering place, or residence; another says a bed and al-Qutaybi a seat. Murtafaq originally means a reclining support, with poetry illustrating its uses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: منزلا. مجاهد: مجتمعا. عطاء: مقرا. وقيل: مهادا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We do not waste the reward’ is parenthetical, not the predicate of ‘those who believe’; the predicate is ‘those will have Gardens of Eden.’ Another analysis supplies an omitted fa.
rows.anchor: ليس قوله: إنا لا نضيع خبرا لقوله: إن الذين آمنوا بل هو كلام معترض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jannāt ʿadn are gardens of abiding residence; rivers run beneath their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر الجزاء فقال: أولئك لهم جنات عدن، ووهي الإقامة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Each person wears three bracelets: one of silver, one of gold, and one of pearls and rubies.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: يحلى كل واحد منهم ثلاثة من الأساور،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine brocade and istabraq thick brocade; some say istabraq is a Persian loanword.
rows.anchor: من سندس، وهو ما رق من الديباج وإستبرق، وهو ما غلظ منه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāʾik are couches in canopies, with arīkah as singular; the gardens are an excellent resting place.
rows.anchor: على الأرائك، وهي السرر في الحجال، واحدتها: أريكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax makes ‘two men’ the object, with an implied comparison: ‘set out for them a parable like two men.’
rows.anchor: رجلين منصوب مفعول، على معنى: واضرب لهم مثلا كمثل رجلين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Identifications differ: Meccan brothers Abu Salama and al-Aswad; Muhammad and Meccan polytheists; Uyayna ibn Hisn and companions compared with Salman and companions; or Israelite brothers with differing names reported for the believer and unbeliever.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أخوين من أهل مكة من بني مخزوم، أحدهما مؤمن وهو أبو سلمة

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: He tells of brothers sharing eight thousand dinars: one gave away a thousand each time the other bought worldly land, a house, wife, or servants, seeking the equivalent in Paradise.
rows.anchor: معمر عن عطاء الخراساني قال: كان رجلان شريكين، وكان لهما ثمانية آلاف دينار،

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: After giving away his share, the believer became needy and asked his wealthy brother for help; the brother rejected him and denied resurrection and recompense. The account links to 37:50–57.
rows.anchor: ثم أصابته حاجة شديدة فقال: لو أتيت صاحبي هذا لعله ينالني منه معروف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vineyards were surrounded by palms, with crops between them.
rows.anchor: بستانين من أعناب وحففناهما: أحطناهما بنخل وجعلنا بينهما زرعا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each garden yielded its full harvest without loss, and a river was split and made to flow through their middle.
rows.anchor: كلتا الجنتين آتت: أعطت، يعني: آتت كل واحدة من الجنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamar may mean abundant wealth or, on another reading, fruits; glosses include gold and silver (Mujahid), types of wealth (Ibn Abbas), all wealth (Qatada), and principal wealth (Ibn Zayd).
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ: (ثمر) فهو جمع ثمرة. مجاهد: ذهب وفضة. ابن عباس: أنواع المال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner is identified as Fatrus; ‘more money and stronger retinue’ means richer in property and stronger in clan, though Qatada says servants and attendants.
rows.anchor: وكان له، يعني: لفطروس ثمر، يعني: المال الكثير المثمر من كل صنف،

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري عن النبي
rows.claim: On the Prophet’s ascent, Abraham asked him to urge his community to plant more in Paradise’s good soil; its planting formula is ‘There is no power or strength except through God.’
rows.anchor: فأتيت أبا أيوب الأنصاري فحدث أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعمرو بن شرحبيل ومسروق وإبراهيم
rows.claim: They identify lasting good deeds as the five prayers and as good deeds that erase sins.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وعمرو بن شرحبيل ومسروق وإبراهيم: هي الصلوات الخمسة،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He lists lasting deeds as testimony, seeking forgiveness, blessing Muhammad, prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, charity, freeing slaves, jihad, kinship, and every good deed enduring for its owner in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: هي الأعمال الصالحة: لا إله إلا الله،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He also glosses them as good speech.
rows.anchor: وروى عطية عن ابن عباس قال: هي الكلام الطيب.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Intentions and aspirations are lasting deeds because actions are accepted and raised through them.
rows.anchor: قال عوف: سألت الحسن عن الباقيات الصالحات، قال: النيات والهمات

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He includes every act intended for God’s approval.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هي كل ما أريد به وجه الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moving the mountains means removing them; Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the verb passively, with ‘mountains’ nominative.
rows.anchor: ويوم نسير الجبال: نزيلها عن أماكنها. وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو:

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: The earth is exposed to sight; Ata says its interior will appear and those buried within will come onto its surface.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: ترى باطن الأرض ظاهرا قد برز الذين كانوا في بطنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone is gathered at the place of reckoning and none is omitted; they stand in rows, or are upright.
rows.anchor: وحشرناهم: جمعناهم إلى الموقف للحساب، فلم نغادر: نترك ونخلف منهم أحدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to disbelievers although its wording is general; coming as first created may mean alive, naked, unarmed, or individually.
rows.anchor: قد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة يعني: أحياء. وقيل: عراة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed time they denied is the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يعني: القيامة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls smiling a small sin and loud laughter a great one; Sa'id includes minor lapses, scratches, kisses, and touching among small sins, and adultery among major sins.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الصغيرة: التبسم، والكبيرة: القهقهة. وقال سعيد بن جبير:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: They explain ‘enumerated it’ as performing, writing and recording, or preserving it; another view says the book counted the deeds.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: عملها. وقال السدي: كتبها وأثبتها. وقال مقاتل بن حيان:

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: When he recited the verse, he said people cried out over small sins before large ones.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم ابن الأشعث: كان الفضيل بن عياض إذا قرأ هذه الآية قال:

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet likened small sins to sticks gathered by travelers: once the pile is kindled, accumulated small sins destroy their owner.
rows.anchor: وضرب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لصغائر الذنوب مثلا فقال:

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: God does not reduce anyone’s reward, punish a person for a crime not committed, or transfer another’s sin to them.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: لا يأخذ أحدا بجرم لم يعمله ولا يورث ذنب أحد على غيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recalls Iblis’s pride to warn the arrogant; his envy and hostility toward humanity resemble the polytheists’ hostility toward Adam’s descendants. Adam’s lapse was disobedience, Iblis’s was pride.
rows.anchor: يقول جل ذكره مذكرا لهؤلاء المتكبرين ما أورث الكبر إبليس،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Iblis belonged to an angelic group called jinn, created from scorching fire, unlike the other angels made from light; his Syriac name was Azazil and Arabic name al-Harith.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كان إبليس من حي من أحياء الملائكة يقال لهم الجن،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says Iblis was Paradise’s treasurer, chief of the lower angels, ruler of the lowest heaven and earth, and unusually forbearing and learned; pride led to rebellion and transformation into a cursed devil.
rows.anchor: وكان اسمه بالسريانية عزازيل وبالعربية الحرث، وكان من خزان الجنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person whose sin is pride should not be expected to repent, whereas repentance may be hoped for when the sin is disobedience.
rows.anchor: فإذا كانت خطيئة الرجل في كبر فلا ترجه، وإن كانت خطيئته في معصية فارجه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not bring Iblis and his offspring, all disbelievers, or—according to al-Kalbi—the heavenly angels to witness creation; He did not need their assistance or counsel.
rows.anchor: ما أشهدتهم: ما أحضرتهم، يعني إبليس وذريته. وقيل: يعني الكافرين أجمع.

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: He reads ashhadhnaahum with the plural nūn and alif of majesty; God did not enlist them as helpers in creation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: (ما أشهدناهم) بالنون والألف على التعظيم،

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads ‘on the day He says’ with nūn; the others read yāʾ, fitting ‘my partners’ rather than ‘our partners.’
rows.anchor: ويوم يقول نادوا قرأ حمزة بالنون. الباقون بالياء لقوله: شركائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawbiqan is interpreted as a deep Hell valley, boiling fluid, a river of fire, enmity, destruction, or an appointed place; its root means ruin.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا بينهم يعني بين الأوثان وعبدتها. وقيل: بين أهل الهدى والضلالة موبقا،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The criminals are polytheists who expect to enter the Fire; other glosses say rush into or descend into it. Al-Aʿmash reads ‘encounter it.’
rows.anchor: ورأى المجرمون: المشركون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها: داخلوها. وقال مجاهد:

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي
rows.claim: A disbeliever sees Hell and thinks he will enter it from a distance of forty years’ travel.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explained every kind of parable in the Quran so people may remember and take heed.
rows.anchor: ولقد صرفنا: بينا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل ليتذكروا ويتعظوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The human is most disputatious’ means persistent argument for falsehood; one view specifies Ubayy ibn Khalaf, another applies it generally.
rows.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا: خصومة في الباطل، يعني أبي بن خلف الجمحي،

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي عن أبيه
rows.claim: When the Prophet woke Ali and Fatima for prayer, Ali said their souls were in God’s hand and He would wake them if He wished; the Prophet left repeating this verse and striking his thigh.
rows.anchor: روى الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب عن أبيه قال: «إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طرقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The alternative is God’s way of destroying earlier peoples; qabulan means visibly, al-Kalbi says the sword at Badr, Mujahid says suddenly, and a doubled-damma reading means kinds of punishment.
rows.anchor: إلا أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين يعني سنتنا في إهلاكهم أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا، قال ابن عباس:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance reaching people is the Quran, Islam, and Muhammad; they were also prevented from seeking their Lord’s forgiveness.
rows.anchor: إذ جاءهم الهدى: القرآن والإسلام ومحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers only bring glad tidings and warnings; disbelievers argue falsely to erase the truth and mock God’s signs and warnings.
rows.anchor: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل ليدحضوا:

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He glosses yudḥiḍū as ‘spoil’; the root means slipping, as in the cited Tarafa verse.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: ليفسدوا، وأصل الدحض: الزلق، يقال: دحضت رجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worst wrongdoer turns away from God’s signs and forgets past sins; covers block understanding of the Quran and heaviness deafens the ears, so such people never accept guidance.
rows.anchor: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه فأعرض عنها: لم يؤمن بها ونسي ما قدمت يداه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness and mercy defer punishment; if He seized people for sins, He would hasten it in this life, but they have an appointed Judgment Day and no refuge.
rows.anchor: وربك الغفور ذو الرحمة لو يؤاخذهم بما كسبوا من الذنوب لعجل لهم العذاب في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawʾilan means a place to turn or refuge; al-Aʿsha’s poem uses yaʾil for escape.
rows.anchor: لن يجدوا من دونه موئلا: معدلا ومنجى، قال الأعشى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns were destroyed for wrongdoing, meaning disbelief, and each destruction had a fixed term.
rows.anchor: وتلك القرى أهلكناهم لما ظلموا: كفروا، وجعلنا لمهلكهم موعدا: أجلا.

none: The segment consists of Quranic verse text without commentary.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After settling Israel in Egypt, Moses listed God’s favors; when asked whether anyone was more learned, he said no. God reproached him for not referring knowledge to Him and directed him to a more learned servant at the junction of the seas, marked by the fish being lost.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما ظهر موسى (عليه السلام) وقومه على مصر أنزل قومه مصر،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another report, God says His beloved remembers Him, the best judge judges justly, and the most learned seeks to add others’ knowledge to his own; that servant is al-Khidr at the shore by the rock.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية أخرى: سأل موسى ربه فقال: «رب أي عبادك أحب إليك؟»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish revived after spring-of-life water touched it, moved in the basket, and entered the sea.
rows.anchor: وعندها عين تسمى ماء الحياة، لا يصيب ذلك الماء شيئا إلا حي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s companion was Joshua son of Nun, son of Ephraim, son of Joseph; others say Joshua’s brother or Moses’s servant.
rows.anchor: صاحبه يوشع بن نون بن إفرائيم بن يوسف. وقيل: فتاه أخو يوشع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā abraḥ means ‘I shall keep going’; the seas are identified as Persian and Roman (Qatada), Tangier (Muhammad ibn Kaʿb), or Africa (Ubayy), and ḥuqub as a long span—eighty years for Ibn Umar, seventy for Mujahid. Another view makes Moses and al-Khidr seas of knowledge.
rows.anchor: لا أبرح: لا أزال أسير حتى أبلغ مجمع البحرين، قال قتادة: بحر فارس والروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Joshua alone forgot the fish, forgetting is attributed to both because they shared the trip and provisions; the author compares this to pearls being attributed to both seas although they come from salt water alone.
rows.anchor: نسيا حوتهما: تركا حوتهما، وإنما كان الحوت مع يوشع، وهو الذي نسيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saraban means a passage or route through which the fish traveled in the sea.
rows.anchor: فاتخذ الحوت سبيله في البحر سربا، أي مسلكا ومذهبا يسرب ويذهب فيه.

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن رسول الله
rows.claim: The water opened into a cavity that stayed open; Moses followed the fish through it and found al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: فروى أبي بن كعب عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «انجاب الماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The fish’s fin-mark remained in clay; everything it touched dried until it became like rock.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رأى أثر جناحه في الطين حين وقع في الماء،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي بن كعب عن رسول الله
rows.claim: They slept at the rock; the fish leapt from its basket, and God held water back like an arch above it. Joshua forgot to tell Moses, and they continued until Moses asked for breakfast the next morning.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن عباس عن أبي بن كعب عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: God restored the fish’s life; its route through the water became frozen and dry.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: رد الله عز وجل إلى الحوت روحه فسرب من البحر

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Joshua’s ablution from the spring of life splashed onto the salted fish, reviving it; its tail movements dried the water it passed through.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: توضأ يوشع بن نون من عين الحياة فانتضح على الحوت المالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses became tired only after passing the rock; hunger was imposed to remind him of the fish and bring him back to his destination.
rows.anchor: ولم ينصب موسى في سفره ذلك إلا يومئذ حين جاوز الموضع الذي أمر به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion may mean ‘I forgot to tell you about the fish’; the clause about Satan has alternate word order and ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فيه إضمار معناه: نسيت أن أذكر أمر الحوت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish’s wondrous route may be Joshua’s statement of amazement or Moses’s response after hearing Joshua’s account.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذا من قول يوشع، يقول: اتخذ الحوت سبيله في البحر عجبا.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He marvels that a piece of fish, eaten over a long time, came alive and was gathered into the sea.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أي شيء أعجب من حوت، كان دهرا من الدهور يؤكل منه

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: The fish left a cleft or trench in the water, like a stream, from its entry to endpoint.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: ظهر في الماء من أثر جري الحوت شق وأخدود شبه نهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That is what we were seeking’ refers to al-Khidr; Moses and Joshua retraced their steps following their tracks.
rows.anchor: ذلك ما كنا نبغ أي نطلب، يعني الخضر فارتدا: فرجعا على آثارهما قصصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant is al-Khidr, whose name is Bilya son of Malkan son of Yaqtan; reports explain his epithet through greenery appearing where he sat or prayed.
rows.anchor: فوجدا عبدا من عبادنا يعني الخضر واسمه بليا بن ملكان بن يقطن،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says al-Khidr was named because white barren ground turned green beneath him; Abd al-Razzaq glosses it as dry vegetation or land with plants.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إنما سمي الخضر خضرا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says al-Khidr was named because the area around him turned green when he prayed.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إنما سمي الخضر لأنه إذا صلى اخضر ما حوله.

rows.speaker: عثمان بن أبي سلمان
rows.claim: He reports that Moses saw al-Khidr on a green mat floating on water and greeted him.
rows.anchor: عن عثمان بن أبي سلمان قال: رأى موسى الخضر (عليه السلام) على طنفسة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي بن كعب عن النبي
rows.claim: Al-Khidr was asleep under a covering; he recognized Moses as Israel’s prophet and said the one who guided Moses had told him who he was.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس عن أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A swallow carried a tiny amount of water; al-Khidr taught Moses that human knowledge is negligible beside God’s, then Moses asked to follow him and learn right guidance.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: وصل إليه وهو يصلي، فلما سلم عليه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks to learn right guidance; al-Khidr says Moses cannot be patient because he acts on inward knowledge God taught him and Moses has not comprehended it. Ibn Abbas says he acted on the unseen.
rows.anchor: قال إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا لأني أعمل بباطن علم علمنيه ربي عز وجل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promises patience, God willing, and obedience.
rows.anchor: قال موسى: ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr tells Moses not to question anything objectionable until al-Khidr first explains it.
rows.anchor: قال: فإن اتبعتني فلا تسئلني عن شيء مما تنكر حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boat crew first thought they were thieves, but the owner recognized prophetic faces; a report says the crew recognized al-Khidr and carried them without payment before he removed a plank.
rows.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «فانطلقا يمشيان على ساحل البحر،

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: They read li-yughriqa with yāʾ and raise ahlahā, making the passengers the subject of ‘drown’; Ibn Masud also reads this way.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة (ليغرق) بالياء المفتوحة (أهلها) برفع اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran means an abominable or strange deed; in Arabic it may mean a grave, intense event, as the cited rajaz verse illustrates.
rows.anchor: لقد جئت شيئا إمرا أي منكرا. قال القتيبي: عجبا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says Moses’s first interruption was due to forgetfulness and the second to destiny; had he waited, God would have told more.
rows.anchor: عكرمة عن ابن عباس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «كانت الأولى

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: He says Moses did not forget; he used an indirect expression.
rows.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب: أما إنه لم ينس، ولكنه من معاريض الكلام.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ‘For what I forgot’ means what Moses omitted from al-Khidr’s instruction; irhaqnī means do not hasten or burden him with difficulty.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: معناه بما تركت من عهدك، ولا ترهقني: تعجلني

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Al-Khidr found boys playing, selected a handsome bright-faced boy, laid him down, and cut his throat; Ibn Abbas says he had not reached puberty.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: وجد الخضر غلمانا يلعبون، وأخذ غلاما ظريفا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says the boy was corrupt and had harmed his parents; other reports name the boy or parents, call him a bandit, and differ on whether he was beheaded, kicked, or struck against a wall.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كان غلاما يعمل بالفساد، وتأذى منه أبواه:

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says the boy killed by al-Khidr was predestined an unbeliever; Moses called him a pure soul.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن أبي بن كعب قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakiyya means pure or Muslim; al-Kisai treats the forms as dialect variants, Abu Amr distinguishes sinless from repentant, and nukran is more severe than imran. ‘Without a soul’ means without killing one warranting retaliation.
rows.anchor: أي طاهرة. وقيل: مسلمة. قال الكسائي: الزاكية والزكية لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says that if he asks again, al-Khidr may end their companionship; he has given al-Khidr an excuse to part.
rows.anchor: قال إن سألتك عن شيء بعدها أي هذه المرة فلا تصاحبني: فارقني

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for Moses and himself, saying that if Moses had stayed with al-Khidr, he would have seen more wonders.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن أبي بن كعب قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies the village as Antioch; Ibn Sirin instead says Aylah and calls it the land farthest from the sky.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني أنطاكية. وقال ابن سيرين: أيلة ، وهي أبعد أرض الله من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The travelers asked for food and lodging, but the people neither fed nor hosted them.
rows.anchor: استطعما أهلها فأبوا أن يضيفوهما، أي ينزلوهما منزلة الأضياف

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet calls the inhabitants miserly; Qatada calls villages that deny guests and wayfarers their rights the worst villages.
rows.anchor: فأبوا أن يضيفوهما قال: «كانوا أهل قرية لئاما» . وقال قتادة في هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: He says the wall was one hundred cubits high; its ‘desire’ to collapse is figurative for being close to collapse. Another view attributes the state to God as wall’s owner, like anger subsiding or a decision being resolved.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: كان جدارا طوله في السماء مائة ذراع، يريد أن ينقض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanqaḍḍ means fall or collapse; Yahya ibn Umar reads yanqāḍ as splitting lengthwise, as with a wall, tooth, or well.
rows.anchor: أن ينقض، أي يسقط وينهدم، ومنه انقضاض الكواكب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem beginning with the poet loading gear beside a camel illustrates the wording of the lattakhadhta reading.
rows.anchor: وقد تخدت رحلي إلى جنب غرزها … نسيفا كأفحوص القطاة المطرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj cites Abu Shamam al-Sababi’s verse about making tools from iron as evidence for the reading’s language.
rows.anchor: وأنشد الزجاج في قوله: (لتخذت) قوله أبي شمام الصبابي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajran means a fee or wage; another view takes it as food, hospitality, or lodging.
rows.anchor: عليه، أي على إصلاحه وإقامته أجرا، أي جعلا وأجرة. وقيل:

rows.speaker: لاحق بن حميد
rows.claim: He reads firāqan with nunation in the statement that their separation is at hand.
rows.anchor: قرأ لاحق بن حميد: (فراق) بالتنوين،

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: He says the boat belonged to ten brothers, five disabled and five who worked at sea.
rows.anchor: قال كعب: كانت لعشرة إخوة: خمسة منهم زمنى، وخمسة منهم يعملون في البحر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the owners miskīn shows ownership does not remove poverty when need exceeds one’s property; such a person may receive zakat. Ibn Abbas says a traveler remains poor even with a thousand dinars.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: لمساكين دليل على أن المسكين وإن كان ملك شيئا فلا يزول عنه اسم المسكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾahum may mean ahead, as in other Quranic uses and a cited poem, or behind them because they would return that way and did not know of the king.
rows.anchor: وكان وراءهم أي أمامهم وقدامهم كقوله تعالى: من ورائه جهنم ومن ورائهم برزخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king seized every sound ship, with ‘sound’ implicit; Ibn Abbas’s reading makes it explicit. Al-Khidr damaged it to save it from the infidel king, whose name varies in reports.
rows.anchor: ملك يأخذ كل سفينة غصبا، أي كل سفينة صالحة، فاكتفى بدلالة الكلام عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashīnā may mean ‘We knew’; Ubayy’s codex reads ‘your Lord feared,’ while Qutrub says ‘We disliked.’ Yarhaqahuma may mean destroy, overwhelm, or burden them with tyranny and disbelief; Sa'id says parental love might lead them to follow the boy’s religion.
rows.anchor: وأما الغلام فكان أبواه مؤمنين فخشينا، أي فعلمنا. وفي مصحف أبي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakātan means righteousness and Islam; qaruban raḥman may mean kinship or mercy. Ibn Abbas says more dutiful to parents, Qatada better, Ibn Jurayj more compassionate, and al-Farra easier for them to love.
rows.anchor: فأردنا أن يبدلهما ربهما خيرا منه زكاة: صلاحا وإسلاما وأقرب رحما

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: God replaced the slain boy with a girl who married a prophet and bore a prophet through whom a nation was guided; another report says she bore seventy prophets.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: أبدلهما الله جارية، فتزوجها نبي من الأنبياء،

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: He says God replaced the boy with a Muslim boy, while the slain boy was an unbeliever; Ubayy’s codex says the slain boy was an unbeliever and his parents believers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: أبدلهما بغلام مسلم وكان المقتول كافرا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The parents rejoiced at his birth and grieved at his death; had he lived he would have ruined them. Believers should accept God’s decree, since what they dislike may be better than what they love.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: قد فرح به أبواه حين ولد وحزنا عليه حين قتل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall belonged to two city orphans, Asram and Sarim; some say the treasure beneath it was scrolls of knowledge (Sa'id ibn Jubayr), while Ibn Abbas says the treasure itself was knowledge.
rows.anchor: وأما الجدار فكان لغلامين يتيمين في المدينة واسمهما أصرم وصريم وكان تحته كنز لهما
